 Meeting Date:  April 30, 2026
 To:  Recreation and Parks Council Liaisons Councilmember Mirisch and
  Councilmember Nazarian
 From:  Michael Muse, Recreation Services Manager
 Subject:  Presentation of the Recreation and Parks Commission Park Bench
  Donation Program

 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
The Park Bench Donation program was developed during the reconstruction of Beverly
Gardens Park in 2015 when the community was looking for opportunities to donate to the
restoration project, give back to the City, while also memorializing their loved ones. The
program then expanded to Roxbury Park shortly after the implementation of the program.
The park bench program is currently set at $5,000 per bench for a total of 10 years. After
10 years, the donor has the option to either rededicate the bench for an additional $5,000
or have the plaque removed and a plaque sent to them.

DISCUSSION
At the February 24, 2026 meeting, staff sought recommendations from the Commission
on any potential changes to the existing park bench donation program but due to time
constraints, the Commission asked to table this item for the March meeting.

At the March 24, 2026 meeting, staff provided follow‑up information on the Park Bench
Donation Program, including an overview of the program’s structure, donation
requirements, and bench availability at Beverly Gardens Park and Roxbury Park.

The Commission suggested reducing the remaining benches at Beverly Gardens Park to
$2,500 and promoting the program in July during Park’s Make Life Better month and at
the Farmer’s Market.
 Meeting Date: April 30, 2026

During the April 28 Recreation and Parks Commission Meeting, staff will seek a vote on
any proposed revisions to the Park Bench Donation program to be brought forward to the
City Council Liaisons.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Park Bench Donation Program is anticipated to be funded by donations from
community members who request a bench to be dedicated. Net positive funds collected
through this program will be transferred to the City’s operating budget for park
programming and maintenance.

RECOMMENDATION
The Recreation and Parks Commission seeks direction and feedback from the Recreation
and Parks Council Liaisons on the proposed commission recommendation for changes to
the Park Bench Donation program.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By

 Meeting Date:  April 30, 2026
 To:  Recreation and Parks Council Liaisons Councilmember Mirisch and
  Councilmember Nazarian
 From:  Michael Muse, Recreation Services Manager
 Subject:  Presentation of the Recreation and Parks Commission’s Proposed
  Adopt-a-Tree Program

 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
At the June 17, 2025, City Council meeting, Council adopted the final City Council
Priorities and Commission Work Plans for fiscal year 2025–26, which included Recreation
and Parks Commission Work Plan items. These workplan items include developing an
Adopt-a-Tree program.

As staff began reviewing an Adopt-a-Tree program, additional complexities and nuances
emerged, necessitating consultation with the City Arborist to provide guidelines and assist
the commission in initiating a conversation.

The City Arborist provided advice that trees will need to be located within the City’s existing
parks. Given ongoing maintenance and changes to the landscape of our parks, the City
Arborist will be required to approve the selected location for each tree before the donation
is accepted. The City Arborist will also be responsible for selecting the tree species and
size that will be procured and planted.

At the February 24, 2026, Commission Meeting, staff sought the Commission's
recommendations on criteria for a tree donation/dedication program. The Commission
provided feedback and requested that staff return in March with additional information and
responses to their questions.
 Meeting Date: April 30, 2026

At the March 24 meeting, staff presented program parameters developed in consultation
with the City Arborist, including guidelines for tree placement, species selection, and
ensuring compatibility with park conditions.

The Commission supported the proposed Adopt-A-Tree program. During the April 28
Recreation and Parks Commission Meeting, staff will seek a vote on the proposed
program, to be brought forward to the City Council Liaisons.

DISCUSSION
At the February 24, 2026, Commission Meeting, staff sought the Commission's
recommendations on criteria for a tree donation/dedication program. The Commission
provided feedback and requested that staff return in March with additional information and
responses to their questions. At the March 24 meeting, staff presented program
parameters developed in consultation with the City Arborist, including guidelines for tree
placement, species selection, and ensuring compatibility with park conditions. The
program framework would support both new plantings and the replacement of aging or
declining trees, with a low‑profile dedication marker recommended to avoid impacts to
green space. Staff also outlined anticipated program costs, including tree procurement,
installation, and long‑term maintenance, with a suggested donation amount of $20,000.

The Commission supported the proposed Adopt-A-Tree program including the proposed
$20,000 donation with the caveat that the price could be reduced if it was deemed to be
inaccessible to the community. The Commission also requested the program include mini
parks as an option for the donors. While the Commission was also in support of the
proposed markers around the tree, they had concerns over potential vandalism and the
tags being cut off.

The commission will vote on a final recommendation during the April 28, 2026 Recreation
and Parks Commission meeting and will be presented during the Liaison Meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Adopt-a-tree program costs will be funded by donations from community members
who request a tree for adoption. Net positive funds collected through this program will be
transferred to the City’s operating budget for park programming and maintenance.

RECOMMENDATION
The Recreation and Parks Commission seeks direction and feedback from the Recreation
and Parks Council Liaisons on the proposed commission recommendation for an Adopt-
A-Tree program.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By

 Meeting Date:  April 30, 2026
 To:  Recreation and Parks Council Liaisons Councilmember Mirisch and
  Councilmember Nazarian
 From:  Michael Muse, Recreation Services Manager
 Subject:  Presentation of the Recreation and Parks Commission Work Plan Items
  for Fiscal Year 2026-27

 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
At the June 17, 2025, City Council meeting, Council adopted the final City Council
Priorities and Commission Work Plans for fiscal year 2025–26, which included Recreation
and Parks Commission Work Plan items. These workplan items include the following
projects:
  1. La Cienega Park Playground Restoration (WP4.3.1)
  2. Large Park Signage & Rules, including Park Safety
  3. Pickleball Pilot Program
  4. Digital Display Review
  5. July Parks Make Life Better – July 4th Community Picnic
  6. Farmers’ Market Programming
  7. Farmers’ Market Rebranding
  8. Library Program Collaboration with BHUSD
  9. Coffee/DJ Program
  10. Collaboration with AYSO/BHLL
  11. Adopt-a-Tree Program
 Meeting Date: April 30, 2026

The Recreation and Parks Commission has completed six (6) of the eleven (11) work plan
items listed above. Completed work plan items include the finalization of the Pickleball
Pilot Program, implementation of digital displays at La Cienega and Roxbury Community
Centers, successful programming of the July 4th Community Picnic, Library programming
collaboration with BHUSD, coffee/DJ programs as part of Mayor Nazarian’s mayoral
initiatives, and continued collaboration with AYSO/BHLL. The La Cienega Park
Playground Restoration is currently underway with anticipated completion this Summer.
The commission and staff have made substantial progress with the large park signage
and rules which will be brought to the liaisons and full City Council in the near future, and
the commission is preparing a final recommendation for the Adopt-a-Tree program.

At the February 24, 2026, Recreation and Parks Commission meeting, the Commission
discussed workplan items for fiscal year 2026-27. As part of that process, the Recreation
and Parks Commission developed and voted on its proposed work plan items for the
upcoming fiscal year. These workplan items include the following projects:

  1.  Safety Call Poles in Parks
  2.  Farmers’ Market Branding and Events (Continued from FY25-26)
  3.  Golf Simulator Program
  4.  Library Tutoring Program Expansion
  5.  Park Lighting Improvements

As outlined at the May 20, 2025 City Council meeting, a revised process was approved to
establish work plans for City commissions with broader discretion in their core
responsibilities, including the Recreation and Parks Commission. Commission work plans
are now brought before City Council for consideration and approval.

The Recreation and Parks Commission will begin that process for their FY 2026-27 work
plan today, in discussion with Council Liaisons and the Recreation and Parks Commission
Chair and Vice Chair.

DISCUSSION
On February 24, 2026, staff guided the Commission to identify proposed priority items for
the 2026-27 workplan. The current work plan is set to expire on June 30, 2026, and the
Recreation and Parks Commission was asked to identify five new or continued priority
items. Each commissioner presented proposed Work Plan items for consideration,
covering a wide range of topics. Following a robust presentation and discussion, the
Recreation and Parks Commission identified the following items for consideration as part
of the proposed work plan:

Safety Call Poles in Parks
Also known as Emergency Call Boxes, these are high-visibility, often blue-lighted,
pedestal-mounted communication devices that provide direct, instant, one-button access
to Police and Dispatchers. The focus of this initiative is enhancing safety within City parks.
Estimated costs range from $3,000 to $15,000 per unit, depending on whether units are
hardwired or solar-powered, as well as installation, foundation, and electrical work
requirements. Staff has initiated conversations with the Information Technology
Department through the City Manager as well as with Beverly Hill Police Department and
will provide insight to their feedback during the presentation.

Page 2 of 3
 Meeting Date: April 30, 2026

Farmers’ Market Branding and Events
This initiative continues last year’s priorities related to the Beverly Hills Farmers’ Market,
with a focus on a redesign of the current Farmers’ Market logo, expanding special events
hosted at the market following changes to the Los Angeles County Health Department
requirements for food related competitions and it’s cost prohibitive nature to the
department and growing the overall scope of the events. Costs are variable depending on
the number of new events and staffing required.

Golf Simulator Program
A golf simulator is a customized indoor system combining a launch monitor, hitting mat,
impact screen, and projector to allow patrons to play virtual rounds of golf or analyze their
swings. This initiative assesses the feasibility of offering this type of programming within
existing City recreation facilities. Estimated costs for a system range from $15,000 to
$50,000 on average.

Library Tutoring Program Expansion
Although the Beverly Hills Public Library is not under the purview of the Commission, it
has been an area where commissioners hear feedback from the community. This project
would explore the possibility of expanding the existing 24-hour online tutoring service by
also providing access to in-person tutors through the City’s library programming. Costs
are currently unknown and will be further evaluated during the planning phase working
closely with the City Librarian for feasibility and implementation.

Park Lighting Improvements
This initiative would enhance overall park lighting by installing improved pathway
illumination to eliminate dark areas and increase safety and visibility for all visitors
throughout City parks. This project aligns with the FY 2026-27 City Council Priority under
Goal 5.1, which includes improving ambient lighting at park sites, particularly La Cienega
Park. Costs are currently unknown and will be further evaluated.

FISCAL IMPACT
Recreation and Parks Commission Work Plan items will be funded through the available
Community Services operating budget for FY 2026–27, where applicable.
Capital improvements, expanded programmatic costs, and any items requiring budget
enhancements will be identified and brought forward to City Council for consideration as
part of the review and approval process of workplan items.

RECOMMENDATION
The Recreation and Parks Commission seeks direction and feedback from the Recreation
and Parks Council Liaisons on the proposed commission work plans for the 2026-27 fiscal
year, to ensure continued alignment with City Council priorities.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By
